I cover a wide range of genres both paid and unpaid, providing unbiased opinions as well as regular giveaway events. [/quote] [b]Video Review[/b] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a3xqHQRVzdo [h2]Revolutionizes Roguelike Deckbuilders[/h2] So if you're not familiar with OTA IMON Studios, they're a group that likes to take risks with their strange and unusual game designs even though their only other game is "WolfStride" which I highly recommend picking up, which incorporates many distinct systems that are both full of character and story, as well as motivational goals and growth rather than 100% random choice and not to mention, dirt cheap for the hours of gameplay available. Putting it in perspective, half the price of Slay The Spire and other such games at 25-30+ or more. When I say random choice, I mean that it gets incredibly boring with Action Roguelikes, especially linear deck builders, where your only purpose is to get to the boss and plot your way to do so safely, but Zet Zillions exploits the idea of. "Hey! We will reward you with AMAZING cards and attributes if you can manage to get here to finish these quests and survive!" This makes traversing each segment of the map chapter much more enjoyable and tension-filled, while also allowing you to go back rather than just forward. It uses the same feature as FTL, the danger zone, which isn't used too often, I'm quite happy to see it reappear in this game since you could risk even more to gain even more cards and power. The soundtrack is as banger as ever! [h2]Colonizing & Combat[/h2] This game approaches things a little differently with combat. You're entire goal is to colonize planets with your population of Meat robots for humanity, which is hilarious because it gives off the same vibe as StarShip Troopers or HellDivers 2 Humanity, where you're fighting for humanity, but in this case you're just a bunch of power hungry overlords attempting to take over the galaxy. When you fully populate a planet it will become stunned, then you erase that population and do it again with cards that grant you tons of damage and reset the value. Certain events have you actually needing to colonize powerful planets to get massive rewards and it's honestly no easy feat with the effects that they have at their disposal. You'll mostly be blowing planets up, which you'll come to want to do, I don't wanna spoil it. [h2]Issues[/h2] If you tend to click things too quickly or not let certain sections of the game load in like the Rescue Pod, etc, the game can and will crash, but the game saves every encounter so while it is annoying to have to log out and back in, it doesn't hinder progression. A handful of other bugs as well that eventually can become game breaking not being able to interact with the event like the Space Dragon and trading cards for currency. One big issue is the danger zone, it does nothing meaning with a shuffle deck you can roam and soak up thousands of pineapples at the end of the stage to buy out the entire shop. His left hand is the only thing that will show up (Thanatos) and the giant mouth does nothing, so that needs to be fixed immediately. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] Zet Zillion is a unique spin on the overcrowded deck building genre expanding on the ideas of Slay the Spire thoroughly. If you've played them all and many others, it seems fresh, unique, and inventive while still being difficult and full of charm and fantastic voice actors, not to mention a very impressionable visual art style that you're sure to love and maybe be a bit scared by (you'll know when you know) haha. Definitely going to love playing this one.

Edit: There are some softlocks that occur, I'm enjoying Zet Zillions but it may be worth waiting a few weeks for those to be ironed out. Worth the price tag if you like the genre. I was genuinely shocked when I saw this was $10. After playing the demo before Zet Zillions' release, I was fully prepared to drop $25. So far the game seems even better than the demo was. Great soundtrack, cool interpretation of FTL's map in a different format, and some great solutions for things like shops. At least in my early runs, I've also had a lot of opportunity to remove a lot of cards, allowing me to really focus each deck onto a specific idea while also letting me drop cards that didn't quite work out. Giving the player enough room for experimentation is great. Excited to see how the game continues to unfold.

4/10分，主打一个废牌转化机制，但转化完了还是废牌，明明有两个数值体系，但是都要过护甲，说白了就是个纯数值游戏，但是数值的成长性却极差。数值的限制来自于手牌上限和费用，简单来说就是策略追求单牌质量，但是占手牌上限的废牌太多，有时为了合并出一张有用的牌要拿更多的废牌，如此看来，最终有用的牌就还是那几张，同一套combo从头玩到尾，combo以外的牌多拿一张都是拖后腿。像极了刚学会做游戏的新手做出来的练手作品，虽然卡牌游戏的美术没什么意义，牌佬不在乎美术，但风格化倒是有些东西，分数全是给美术的。

Zet Zillions, made by the creators of Wolfstride, is a very similar kind of game. That is to say, its stylish, cool and completely shallow. ZZ is a roguelite deckbuilder, but most of unlockable starting bonuses are only obtained after you've beaten the final boss. I unlocked Gilgamesh's Eye, the second companion, on the same run that I killed Super Duper Thanatos, or whatever his name is. I haven't even unlocked any of the other starting cards (like Frag-a-Jam). In addition, most of the cards that you can add to your deck are quite ♥♥♥♥, meaning that only a few strategies are properly good. The game has a fair few gamebreaking bugs (one time in act 3 I got booted to the map instead of act 4 when I beat the boss of the area), and another time I crashed everytime I tried to go to a mission planet. The base mechanic is fun: fuse your cards together to do cool ♥♥♥♥. The problem is that you don't know what fuses with what. This unicorn thing, what do I fuse it with? This bomber plane thing, what do I fuse that with? You'll only know when you add to your deck, which results in adding ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards that don't work with your build. Instead, just add deal 15 + 15 population for 2 cost. That ♥♥♥♥ is useful 100% of the time. Fusion is a cool idea, but it rarely does anything really strong and its impossible to know how it works. Another thing that really needs improving is the art. The art is great, super cool, when its completed. Many cards, like the various event pets, don't have finished art, most of them have only a placeholder sketched art. The game is hilariously short, I beat it in 6 hours. Not like, won my first run, no I beat the final boss over multiple runs in a measly 6 hours. Tl;dr: cool idea. bad execution. There's almost no substance. If you want to sell a game for 20 dollars, try making the game better. This game could be good, it just isn't.

牌的种类少，给玩家提供的强化很少，难度曲线高，没有让人玩下去的欲望 （几乎）什么都可以组合？ 是可以组合 玩家认为的：每张卡合成都会变成不一样的卡 实际上：不管什么卡基本合出来的卡几乎都一样（而且很垃圾），就那么两张 敌人有护甲（回合结束不会消失！），你可以往敌人上面甩人口，但是先得破甲 人口牌单独打-5甲，护甲牌＋人口牌合成打出去-7甲，难道合成的卡很强？ ？地点大概率遇敌，敌人也不是只有一个而是多个且都有护甲，这就很恶心了 到后面我拿着一堆垃圾卡，合出来的也是垃圾卡，体验感极差！ 3/10分 给美术磕个头吧，不然真不想玩下去
星际版爬塔。画风个顶个得有趣，任务系统也让人眼前一亮。卡牌融合系统、“人口”系统算是本作玩法上的特色和创新点，值得尝试的DBG新作！评分：4/5分！
不推荐。 养成太慢，一直在玩初始卡组。 卡牌的融合机制重复度非常高，看似有庞大的融合组合，实际上融合结果非常少。

It looks stylish, but it's just not much fun. Since you aren't discarding at the end of each turn like most deckbuilders, there's no interesting choice in which cards to play. Combining cards sounded like a neat idea, but there were very few different results, so it never felt particularly useful. None of the cards I saw felt like much mattered beyond "Is the number bigger" And also the game felt sluggish to respond and difficult to read visually. After the bombastic opening, I was very disappointed.

目前不推荐，里面首先所有行星位置给什么都是不明确的，除非是事件和任务，其次就是游戏里的追赶太蠢了，过图纯看运气然后后面还有一个在追你，把你走过的和旁边的路线全部清空，虽然可以理解为和别的游戏的分路是类似的，但差就差在完全未知以及过关的和能选择的奖励真的很少，想要组一套有配合的卡组基本不可能，跟别说别的游戏那种永动组合或是机制配合的卡组，这游戏基本组不出来，而且不知道为什么我都通关好多次了，第二套卡组还是不解锁，一直玩第一套也没有说明怎么解锁第二套，还有就是游戏里卡牌融合的机制，看上去很新颖其实很鸡肋，游戏里目前我遇到的卡牌种类：废料人、垃圾、小队、生物、行动、武器，有些卡牌明明同样是武器类型的，这一张只能和废料人融合，那一张只能和垃圾融合，完全没有规则和逻辑，每一张都要去试，根本无法在选牌和买牌的时候知道这张卡适不适合我的卡组。

现在又更新了新的剧情还有boss，未来可期！ 6月1日，能够正常游玩了，升到15级没有解锁第三套初始牌组，但是经验获取翻倍了？！但是我已经满级了（悲）不过制作组态度可以，好评:D 2024年5月31日，遇到恶性bug了，选完初始牌组开始旅程就会卡死，我电脑直接卡死，试了关机重启再进游戏，3次全都卡死，很逆天！距离15级还差2000左右经验，我是急急急急急急国王，这个bug修复了还是换回好评，毕竟玩了好久好久，希望更新更多的内容增强可玩性 已经通关最终boss战，但还是没解锁第二套卡组，是没有更新吗？我的打法就是一路炸炸炸，所以不是很难。而且如果你觉得自己快要输了可以Esc小退一下游戏，再重新开始这场战斗（ps我就是用这方式打了最终boss好几遍才打过）我推测要完成那个角色的任务可能会解锁相应的卡组，或者把卡组1升到满级？？？打算之后试试，不行的话那初始卡组玩到死，那真的别太离谱。附：升到14级解锁了新的初始牌组2，太漫长了吧！建议更改一下，过于离谱 总的来说有新鲜感，内容不是特别多吧，好多融合都不太敢尝试，看样子貌似也不太行。如果打折力度比较强，用来杀杀时间还是可以的，不用想那么多，直接炸炸炸，给他们爆了！不算太优秀，但还是推荐推荐

[h1]《狂星滥炸》：氛围拉满的美漫风卡牌[/h1] 《狂星滥炸》是一款由OTA IMON Studios开发、Raw Fury发行的卡牌游戏，就像我在不久前的评测里把《幽灵霍迪》称作「花瓶游戏」一样，本作也有那么点”花瓶卡牌“的意思。但肉眼可见的一点在于，它的美术真的很优雅，让你看到了就移不开眼睛那种。 说到OTA IMON Studios这个制作组，它们最初给玩家留下印象的作品是《迅狼疾步》，而在那部黑白风格的像素游戏中就已经给玩家展示了它们强烈的美术风格，以及充满着张狂特性的美漫气质，粗犷的线条与黑白像素块糅杂在一起有一种奇妙的和谐感。到了这次的《狂星揽炸》中，黑白世界被赋予了颜色，也更加能凸显美漫作品的优势，个性鲜明的大色块互相碰撞，代表了一种肆虐的不羁与狂放。而这个中文标题《狂星滥炸》我觉得也翻译的十分信达雅，至少非常贴合作品气质。 除了画面的整体视效亮眼，作品在敌人的造型设计上也十分考究，不需要几次战斗单凭借外形就能给你留下深刻印象。各种战斗特效和伤害显示也是拉满了，打起来手感丝滑不说，看着各种扭曲的敌人在他们的脸上疯狂蹂躏也颇有满足感，反馈感十足，可以说在美术的方方面面我都挑不出什么毛病。 至于游戏玩法上，不仅有《杀戮尖塔》的底层逻辑，也有些”看起来很新的东西“。事件树借用了尖塔的框架，不过把树状结构变成了网状、并且玩家可以再次前往已经探索过的地点，只不过事件会发生变化，也算是有一点新奇的体验。 另一个独特设计在于「人口」机制。游戏里存在一种与血量并行的人口系统，与把”敌人星球化“互相配合，成为一套逻辑自洽的战斗体系。在战斗过程中，你可以通过卡牌效果不断把敌人的人口叠满，这样会使得敌人进入一回合的眩晕状态，方便我方进行后续输出；同时游戏里也有一些任务目标是对敌人进行“殖民”，也就是把敌人的人口数量叠到上限，围绕着炸个崭新的机制确实也玩出了不少花样。 不过总的来说，游戏的数值和深度都略显不足，虽然融合卡牌的玩法有趣、人口机制的加入也略显新颖，整体来看仍旧是美术大于Gameplay的养眼作品，因此目前口碑表现一般也就可以理解了。但本作至少做出了创新，并且在美术方面拥有着得天独厚的优势，只要通过不断更新来填补内容上的不足，我觉得未来应该会获得更高的评价。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]
很好的开局体验，但也仅限于开局。 数值崩坏，事件数量少，钱几乎没有用处、因为商店就是个摆设！还有bug，我直接在第4章结尾卡死，坏档。 更蠢的是，游戏内容极其之少，开局就一个角色一个初始卡组，通关了3次也没有解锁更多。看样子这游戏就一个角色，不过是有3套不同的开局卡组而已，蠢爆了。

So stylish. Art is such a trip. So cool. The trash and junk Love the story, ENGAGING, QUALITY voice acting. Characters and dialog are legit funny. Cool mechanics. Love the population and the different quests and how it ties into the cards you get... Tons of ways to ditch cards, get cards, just a super satisfying deck building in the BUILDING sense. Just not enough variation or meta progression. The UI sugggggesssttsss I'll get a different deck. But I don't. Maybe i'll go back to finish the story one day but I'm not running the same thing 4 times when I know I'm going to be able to steamroll it again. Card unlocks are slow and honestly a pet peeve in the genre -- 1 or 2 cards per run doesn't change ♥♥♥♥. Give big batches of related synergy cards and abilities, not efficiency-cards as meta progression. Its not changing the experience at all. No signs of more challenge or modes... Such a nice 3 runs but that's all that's here? More meat required on the (really awesome) bones. At least some difficulty settings? Maybe I'm cutting too soon but that's my critique -- I don't want to do the same thing again.
just a ok game, not very addictive

一款以剧情驱动的肉鸽卡牌游戏，游戏优秀的视听元素能够给玩家留下深刻的印象，但打牌上的游戏性不足就很难让他成为这个品类下的真正佳作。 如果你是追求打牌游戏性的硬核“牌佬”，那么这款游戏或许并不能满足你。但如果你是被游戏的美术所吸引，并且对打牌和肉鸽的元素要求偏低，那么这款游戏还是非常值得尝试的。 亮点： ·充满特色的美式漫画风格 ·诙谐幽默的游戏文本 ·有趣的机制设计 雷点： ·卡牌及卡组解锁过慢 ·卡牌构筑单一，深度不足 ·全程加载及动画偏慢影响体验 ·部分不人性化的设计

[h1] Bundle of Fun, But...[/h1] [i]Review written [b]after[/b] the major 1.5 Patch released on July 19th. The campaign has been finalized, launch issues (slow progression) were sorted, many UI complaints were addressed, and some cards were balanced. There are/were 3 major decks accessible as of this point and 3 secondary 'deck' options at this point, leaving roughly ~9 options to start a game with.. though you do just start with 1 major and 1 secondary by default.[/i] [b]TLDR[/b]: [i]Game Experience[/i] is fun, unique gimmick is intuitive, and art is gorgeous. [i]Gameplay[/i] is bittersweet and short. Zet Zillions is a genuinely novel deckbuilder experience with catchy music, silly humor, and interesting gameplay. It's greatest issues are found in its humor and its short nature. It is still a fun game experience first and foremost. The humor will bother those who dislike, or are offended, by juvenile stuff. For example, you simultaneously are fighting pirates, space bugs, angry planets, cosmic monsters, and [i]giant space turds[/i]. For deckbuilder fans, equate the gimmick of the turds to encounters/enemies that fill your deck with curses and dilute your card draw. They have a mechanical purpose. I found it funny and silly. The short nature is a problem for the mechanical deckbuilder purist who values 100's of hours of gameplay over a gameplay experience. You will likely be 100% done with this game at 15-20 hours max. Sooner if you do not game over or just focus on using the same strategy that wins you your first run. [h2] Very Enjoyable If... [/h2] ... you are looking for: [list] [*] [b]A Fun Deckbuilder.[/b] There are various distinct strategies that can lead to victory. A current top review says there are limited strategies, but I do not believe that was true before the 1.5 patch, and especially not after. The patch was released July 19th. This isn't a flame of that review though since the unlock pace of new content at launch was silly slow, whereas now that has been adjusted significantly. [*][b]Studio Trigger Artstyle.[/b] Look, if you know you know. And if you know and do not see it you may be blind. [*][b]A Novel Experience.[/b] The entire package of the interesting mechanics, art, campy story, voice acting, and bopping music is a complete package. Everything was put together with one vision and experience in mind. It is short and simple. [*][b]Something Just Fun[/b] I touched on it a little with the last point, but the game just wants to be fun. There is occasional serious plot stuff, but its tone as a whole is absurd and goofy. Look at the steam page art, you should see exactly what I mean. [*][b]A Cool Gimmick.[/b] The gimmick is fusion, which lets you combine two different cards in your hand. You can drag two different cards together and get a special card. In StS terms, imagine if you could combine a strike and block temporarily into a third card. Maybe it gives energy, draws, inflicts a debuff, or whatever. Combining is free, but you still need to pay for the resulting card. If the gimmick seems bad, your deck may not support fusion or have good fusions. [/list] [h2]May Not Be Enjoyable If... [/h2] ... you are looking for: [list] [*] [b]Longevity.*[/b] There is no ascension or prestige system... yet? The team is talking about a challenge mode that may target this exact comment. Depending on its implementation [i]and if[/i] it has some fun gimmicks, small amounts of new enemies, or something special that could change things up. [*][b]A Pure Deckbuilder.[/b] There is narrative system which treats each run as a chapter. Often, that means ending it with a boss as you'd want and expect. Some sort of obstacle. There are also different bosses. Other times it may just be a free win without a boss... or a boss rush. The pure deckbuilder player enjoys focusing on the run, having some obstacles, and will enjoy one or more bosses. But a run ending with no boss because story is probably lame after you set up a super sick deck. Depending on the nature of challenge mode, this may not matter, but yeah. [*][b]A Serious Game.[/b] The game is silly, and I enjoy that. I mentioned the space turds, but there is other silly things like fighting planets by trying to colonize them before they kill you(cool)... and the same colonize mechanic is used to also swarm non-planets so you can stun them for one turn. Your initial signature move (starter deck) can detonate all of the trash (thats what the colonizer units are called, they are actually not humans) to do massive damage. There is actual strategy behind the jokes and naming conventions, but I [i]know for certain[/i] some people don't want any silly stuff in their games.[/list] [h2] What I Want [/h2] For its price, it is easily a valuable $10 experience since I like Trigger style art, the music was sweet, the gameplay was novel, and I got to win with multiple archetypes (discard, poison/burn, big deck, shuffle poison/burn, pulverize, etc). There were some stinkers and deck building traps, but the number of viable picks outweighed those. By the time I started to think critically about the balance, I was nearing the end of the campaign, and had gotten my value from the game. That being said, if there were more chapters (different captain/story/crew) or a genuinely interesting challenge mode (new archetypes, cards, bosses, events, and/or interesting balance/progression) that would be great. A continuation, even if that is silly, would still make me laugh if I got to see credits every two chapters after the story 'ended' each time. Would remind me of MGS5, and seeing 'Kojima' in the opening credits of each mission every-time. But, elaborating further: [list] [*]DLC for the former would be totally fine if it had similar production and new mechanics. I'd still want whatever it added to be transferable to the upcoming challenge mode. [*]A patch for the latter with post-launch would make the most sense. If there was additional stuff included for challenge mode, I'd want it to cater towards the more purist style player who wants to push limits... without relying on a single broken strategy. [/list] Regardless, fun game!

Wow. Oozing style. Yes, it's a roguelike deckbuilder, but the elevator pitch is that in this hyper-stylish game, you're fighting planets/giant enemies, you can fuse cards, and you use "population" as a stagger mechanic. Is it enough? Yes. Fooooor a few hours. There's a game breaking bug that forces you to exit the game, then come back. Unfortunately, unlike other games in the genre, your in-battle progress isn't saved. This game breaking bug is related to the discard mechanic and occurs nearly every battle. No joke. (Specifically, the bug prevents the mouse from interacting with any object, so you can't play cards or end turns) Finally, JFC who wrote this script? I love love love that there are stylized, splashy characters who actually have a voice. But that voice is...grating. sO rAnDom!! cOw LOL! This game could really be a top contender if they eliminated game breaking bugs, added in different more starter deck options and hired an actual script writer (please on this last one - it's dangerously close to unbearable). Not recommending because of the game breaking bugs. Expect 10ish hours of gameplay before you've had enough.

The game has some fun ideas, but I found the implementation to be lacking. Major problems include: [b]Poor information when picking rewards.[/b] Basic rules like "exhaust" are explained, but if a reward has an effect that "creates card [CardName]" the game doesn't show you the created card. Most other deckbuilders include this information in the rewards details overlay. [b]Combination mechanic ruined by tedium.[/b] Combining cards to make new stuff is a great concept but the vast majority make the same 3 or 4 useless cards and it's frustrating checking every combo hoping for something useful. The Gaia's Altar event is even worse. You permanently combine 3 cards and 99% of all combos come out "dungman" with zero indication of what might produce something different. [b]Deckbuilding choices are unrewarding.[/b] Damage and population cards generally don't help each other, so a big chunk are worthless based on your build. Finding useful cards that are more than simplistic "damage/population/block" output is extremely rare. As a result deckbuilding feels limited and combat uninteresting. [b]Bosses hard counter certain builds.[/b] Summons with taunt and thorns crush damage decks not built around big one-hitters. Wiping population every turn means a population decks require a one-turn combo rather than a cumulative approach. A forced learning loss vs a boss isn't the worst thing, but replaying a sector with limited build options amplifies the deckbuilding problems making an irritating situation much worse.

I got this before I knew about Slay the Spire and having just completed Slay the Spire, I have to say Zet Zillions is the better game, better Art, better gameplay loop, has good music, voice acting and a story and yet compared to the massive success of Slay the Spire, the game that inspired Zet Zillions and is referenced in-game even, Zet Zillions barely made a mark. You're an unnamed Clone Commander ('Trash') that has to guide a space Ship Planet through a galaxy (Slay the Spire Roguelike Deckbuilder) while a being called Thanatos gives chase, the cast is whacky and over the top and definitely anime inspired and what seems like a simple gameplay loop as trying to complete the map and clear the boss, where losing time loops you back to the start, expands into Gurren Lagann levels once you start beating the bosses and the story starts to progress. You'll learn about the cast, the villains and have to deal with lots of Pineapples and help knock-off Goku find love. I can't claim it's as complex as Slay the Spire, but If you like Slay the Spire, I'd suggest giving it a play.

优点： 1、画风狂野独特，美术很好，角色全语音，过剧情有点意思。 2、独特的人口机制，把对面的人口堆满就能眩晕敌方一回合，有种打动作游戏的感觉，也能一次性引爆人口造成极高的伤害。 缺点： 1、最终boss一开始就在屁股后面追着，不能往后走，因为他是几个方向追过来，所以预定路线有些地方不能走过去，一边走的太远了，另外一边没去过的地方就会被最终boss摧毁，有一定压迫感，不能全部地方走完获取全部的资源，但是前期敌方的数值有点高，全部走完战损也很大。 2、随机任务很奇葩，好用的东西都是离你很远，跑过去还得怕被最终boss围堵，毕竟这玩意击败了还是会复活，不会说就停在原地不需要担心他从其他地方过来把你要走的地点给摧毁了。 3、卡牌融合机制也很特别，在手上融合不消耗费用，同时由于回合结束是不会丢弃手牌，避免了融合卡牌后由于费用不够打不出又被弃牌的尴尬。但是要融合就意味着要大卡组，不同种类的卡一多就影响卡组运转，那就非常容易卡手。有些卡需要融合的种类是固定的，卡组大了也不一定能抽到想要的融合卡，一直卡在手里达到上限虽说不会丢牌，但是也不抽卡了就很麻烦。 4、部分天赋还要分敌人类型，但是图上的战斗都是未知，不知道敌人类型甚至不知道是普通敌人或者是精英敌人，这种天赋拿了等于没拿。 5、商店极其没用，第一幕还没有，从第二幕开始需要走五步之后才能开启，虽说开启之后直到打当前章节boss前都能随意进入一次，但是商店卖的东西又太费，要价又高，而且还不卖天赋就很搞笑了。 综合来说，这个游戏打折的时候入手尝尝鲜味道不错。

So, after letting this sit on my wishlist for a while, I caught it on sale for a *really* cheap amount - and for the amount I paid, the value has been absolutely off the charts. This is basically FTL meets any of the dozens of card battler style games out there...if the art and humor came from the same general area as Hazbin Hotel and the gameplay difficulty went from "cute, easy, fun" to "jfc, are there cheat codes?" The story isn't much to write home about, but all of the sound and voice acting is excellent. Strategy has a lot of depth to it and the build were varied, though I did default to a guide to finish off the last boss. If there's any complaint I do have, it's that I encountered a couple bugs - menus that wouldn't load, getting stuck in choices that won't allow you to progress because you literally can't fulfill the onscreen choices, and the really random temporary lock up that just...took a couple minutes to resolve. Ultimately, for the price I paid for it (less than $5), this is in the "highly recommended, zero caveats" area. Even at less than $10, I'd still stick it at highly recommended. Lot of fun, definitely flying under the radar - could see it being a kind of cult classic in a couple years.

After successfully beating the game, I can confidently say that Zet Zillions is a breath of fresh air for the genre. If you are tired of standard, repetitive card games, this game absolutely rules with its insane card variety, deep fusion systems, and hyper-aggressive mechanics that let you build completely broken decks. The gameplay loop of weaponizing planet populations and slamming massive monsters into enemies is incredibly addictive, especially when combined with its vibrant, quirky retro-anime art style and punchy animations. Once your deck synergy finally "clicks" in the late game, the power trip is immensely rewarding all the way to the final boss. It’s a fast-paced, stylish masterpiece that delivers tons of strategic depth and replayability!

One of my favorite art styles for a game I've played. So many cool design choices are seen in the planets, bosses, etc. The sense of scale is shown well too. It feels epic fighting something 1000x larger than you. The art mixed with the amazing voice acting really makes it feel like a game woven into an animated show (music was pretty good too). The story was also surprisingly well-done. Although it involves a lot of "wanting to destroy the universe", the strength of the main cast and the villains makes each story segment fun and intriguing to experience. I loved doing random stuff with the main crew, and my focus intensified whenever [spoiler] Trash Zero [/spoiler] or [spoiler] Nix [/spoiler] showed up. Each character was tropey, but it made them all the more lovable. Also [spoiler] Trash Zero [/spoiler] especially was such a cool-ass villain (some insane voice acting and a captivating back story made for such a sick presence). Learning more about the characters and world built up a truly memorable setting. The gameplay was definitely addicting, but I'd say it was my least favorite part of the experience. Not to say it's bad (it's still fun), but everything else was just so good. There are some cool mechanics, and it's enjoyable to use weird cards and builds. I just quickly found a build that worked and kept using it because it felt like the bosses were VERY punishing (White Dwarf is my #1 enemy). I personally didn't find it fun building towards a deck that fails at the final boss because of some particular mechanics it has. I went from struggling and dying a lot to steamrolling everything, even that [spoiler] "boss rush" in chapter 6 [/spoiler]. But I'm also not a big fan of roguelike gameplay loops, so if you do enjoy the 40-minute trial and error and finding a build that kills everything, then you might love it. All things considered, I'm glad I played it, and I wish it got more traction for how well-crafted it is. Can't wait to see what else the dev creates (or how they expand the universe of this game). I hope the next game involves more COWS for my boy Ziggy!

The art and presentation are great but it is wasted on a game that for the most part feels unfinished. The game is ruined by bugs and bad design choices including but not limited to: [list] [*] The fusion mechanic being poorly explained and what cards fuse into what being a archaic mystery until you actually add them to your deck. This makes it hard to gauge what the consequences of putting a card in your deck could be until you actually pick it - kind of important that this would not be the case if you are making a roguelike [b]deckbuilder[/b]. [*] Fights sometimes keep going even after all enemies are defeated. [*] The game randomly deciding whether cards are discarded at the end of the turn or not on a fight by fight basis. [*] Cheap UI design and poor menu controls, together with other gameplay issues making the game tiresome to play. [/list] It feels like for whatever reason the production of this was rushed and the end product suffers a lot because of it.
